finalText:
This is a small Node HTTP API — five files, no dependencies.

```mermaid
graph LR
  A[server.js] -->|checks token| B[auth.js]
  A -->|sends request| C[routes.js]
  C --> D[cache.js]
  C --> E[store.js]
  D --> E
```

- **`server.js`** — the front door. Checks the bearer token on every request, then hands it off.
- **`auth.js`** — makes and checks those tokens. Format is `userId.signature`, signed with a shared secret from `AUTH_SECRET`.
- **`routes.js`** — a small table mapping `METHOD /path` to a handler. Three routes: get a user, list orders, add an order.
- **`cache.js`** — a 256-entry LRU sitting in front of reads, no expiry of its own.
- **`store.js`** — the actual data, kept in memory, each record expiring 15 minutes after its last write.

One thing worth knowing: the comment in `routes.js` says writes should invalidate the cache, but `putOrder` never does that. So after someone adds an order, `GET /orders` can keep serving the stale cached list for a while.
